The app worked. Nobody, including me, had checked whether it was safe.  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

I VIBE CODED A SECURITY RISK https://every.


THE APP WORKED. NOBODY, INCLUDING ME, HAD CHECKED WHETHER IT WAS SAFE. https://every.

by Katie Parrott https://every.

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSSBWaWJlIENvZGVkIGEgU2VjdXJpdHkgUmlzayIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0MDUsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL2FjY291bnQiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6NX0= to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



“The feature is live lol.”

This sentence is not a combination of words I thought I’d ever use, especially about something I built. That “lol” is a 100 percent organic, all-natural millennial nervous lol. I wasn’t laughing. The agent reviewing my code wasn’t either. It had just told me that the feature I had put into my app had to come down while we figured out whether it had exposed a security problem.

Hi, I’m a baby vibe coder https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSSBWaWJlIENvZGVkIGEgU2VjdXJpdHkgUmlzayIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0MDUsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL3dvcmtpbmctb3ZlcnRpbWUvaXQtcy1tZS1oaS1pLW0tdGhlLXZpYmUtY29kZXIiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6Nn0=. You’re probably wondering how I got here. The answer is a rich stew of factors: imagination and ignorance, hubris and—because how could it not—AI.

This past January, as Claude Opus 4.5 https://every. was blowing everyone’s minds and agent-native architecture https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSSBWaWJlIENvZGVkIGEgU2VjdXJpdHkgUmlzayIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0MDUsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL2d1aWRlcy9hZ2VudC1uYXRpdmUiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6OH0= was starting to emerge as a new paradigm for building software, I felt the urge to vibe code: What if I built an app designed to work directly with AI agents?

Reader, I did. My app Tastemaker lets you collect clips from writing you admire, describe what you like about them, and generate a style guide https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSSBWaWJlIENvZGVkIGEgU2VjdXJpdHkgUmlzayIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0MDUsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL2d1aWRlcy9ob3ctdG8tYnVpbGQtYW4tYWktc3R5bGUtZ3VpZGUiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6OX0= from the patterns. Once it appeared to be working, with all the pride of a preschooler bringing her fingerpainting home for mom to put on the fridge, I bought a domain and unleashed it into the world.

The app worked. People could use it. To my astonishment, a handful of people actually did. It became a small, live monument to my multi-hyphenate abilities: proof that I had become a writer-builder with a real-live product, rather than a writer with product ideas.

And then, like a preschooler left alone with her creation and an open bottle of paint, I went and ruined the whole thing.

Researchers at OpenAI have a name for what I was doing as I fiddled with API keys, Supabase (a backend database service I barely understand), and a whole basket of vocabulary words I’d first heard a year ago. They call it task crossover https://every.: using AI to do work historically associated with another occupation. In their analysis of more than 800,000 work-related ChatGPT messages, 16.8 percent involved task crossover.

Somewhere, there are marketers debugging websites, small-business owners reviewing contracts, and other writers looking at a working app and thinking: Well, if I can do this, what else can I do?

For me, the answer turned out to be: enough to get myself into trouble.

You can see the appeal. A person with a specific problem no longer has to find the specialist who might solve it, make the case that the problem deserves their time, and wait for it to make its way to the top of their to-do list. AI can help us make something before it gives us the ability to tell whether it is safe or ready for other people.

Let me tell you my tale of woe.


THE BEGINNER’S HUBRIS

Tastemaker was a place to collect writing I loved and turn my opinions about it into something I could use. I had spent years doing versions of this manually: copying sentences into notes apps, underlining lines in books, and trying to explain why one paragraph had electricity and another had the emotional texture of an onboarding email.

Then I had one more idea.

I wanted people to connect their Tastemaker profile directly to Claude Code, Codex, or whatever agent they were using, so the agent could retrieve their style guide, once they had one, and add new samples without sending them from their agent back to Tastemaker. The technical word for this, which I was just aware enough of to ask for by name, is an MCP: a way for an AI agent to connect to an outside service. (I want it on the record that I thought of it before I knew we were adding something similar to Every’s writing agent, Spiral https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSSBWaWJlIENvZGVkIGEgU2VjdXJpdHkgUml

**1/ Astra could reportedly launch this month with 10 trillion parameters:** Reports suggest OpenAI is preparing to release its next flagship model, codenamed [Astra](https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2085801349866729975?s=20) (very likely to be GPT-6), in August with potentially around 10 trillion parameters. The company reportedly suspended the release yesterday over security concerns. OpenAI has designated Astra as its first “[critical](https://openai.com/index/responding-next-frontier-critical-cyber-capabilities)” cybersecurity-capable AI, triggering stricter safeguards before a broader release. The model can reportedly find and create zero-day vulnerabilities and carry out cyberattacks autonomously, prompting heightened security restrictions and deeper government and third-party testing.

**2/ OpenAI is reportedly preparing an even larger model called Doug: **Another model, reportedly codenamed [Doug](https://x.com/ChrisGPT/status/2086220662264250764?s=20), could arrive by November and is said to be powerful enough to make Anthropic’s [Fable](https://www.anthropic.com/claude/fable) look “primitive.” According to the report, Doug will be OpenAI’s largest pre-training project ever and is separate from GPT-6.

**3/ Meta releases Muse Glimmer for local AI agents:** Meta released [Muse Glimmer](https://x.com/AIatMeta/status/2086757844544811485?s=20), a 30B open-weight model designed for always-on agents running locally on a Mac or PC with a single consumer GPU. Licensed under Apache 2.0, it supports tool use, multi-step reasoning, coding, screenshots, and 100+ languages, while quantization brings it under 20GB of memory for consumer hardware.

newsletters.title: Designing With AI? Make a Jig.
newsletters.content:
The custom tools we created for ‘Before the Deluge’—and what they tell us about the state of AI design  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

DESIGNING WITH AI? MAKE A JIG. https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiRGVzaWduaW5nIFdpdGggQUk_IE1ha2UgYSBKaWcuIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDQwMiwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vcC9kZXNpZ25pbmctd2l0aC1haS1tYWtlLWEtamlnIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjF9


THE CUSTOM TOOLS WE CREATED FOR ‘BEFORE THE DELUGE’—AND WHAT THEY TELL US ABOUT THE STATE OF AI DESIGN https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiRGVzaWduaW5nIFdpdGggQUk_IE1ha2UgYSBKaWcuIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDQwMiwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vcC9kZXNpZ25pbmctd2l0aC1haS1tYWtlLWEtamlnIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjJ9

by Jack Cheng https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiRGVzaWduaW5nIFdpdGggQUk_IE1ha2UgYSBKaWcuIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDQwMiwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vQGphY2tjaGVuZyIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjozfQ==

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiRGVzaWduaW5nIFdpdGggQUk_IE1ha2UgYSBKaWcuIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDQwMiwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vYWNjb3VudCIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo0fQ== to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



One thing I’ve learned as an amateur woodworker is that when a job is difficult to do precisely—or tedious to do repeatedly—you make a jig. A jig, by its broadest definition, is a tool that makes it easier to make something else.

If you’re building a bookcase with adjustable shelves, you need to drill two straight, evenly spaced rows of holes. If you’re making a set of drawers, you need to cut the same interlocking joints again and again. Jigs make jobs like these simpler, more accurate, or both. They constrain the position or movement of a tool or workpiece, making consistent results less dependent on a steady hand. A shelf-pin jig guides a drill from hole to hole; a dovetail jig guides a router through every joint. Jigs can be as simple as a block of wood or as elaborate as a custom-built metal guide.

Jigs are also finding their way into AI-assisted interface design. I first saw the term used in this way by Josh Puckett https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiRGVzaWduaW5nIFdpdGggQUk_IE1ha2UgYSBKaWcuIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDQwMiwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vam9zaHB1Y2tldHQubWUvIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjV9, the cofounder of the design studio Iteration and creator of Interface Craft https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiRGVzaWduaW5nIFdpdGggQUk_IE1ha2UgYSBKaWcuIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDQwMiwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vd3d3LmludGVyZmFjZWNyYWZ0LmRldi8iLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6Nn0=, a growing library of user interaction tools and knowledge. Puckett is also, perhaps unsurprisingly, a hobbyist woodworker himself, who sees many similarities between building furniture and building software.

“To make more advanced and creative things, you have to make tools to help you make the thing,” he told me. “Sometimes you’re like, ah, God, I need an extra pair of hands. That’s where jigs really come into it.”

Designing and producing Every’s interactive piece about OpenAI’s infrastructure team https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiRGVzaWduaW5nIFdpdGggQUk_IE1ha2UgYSBKaWcuIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDQwMiwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vcC9vcGVuYWktaW5mcmFzdHJ1Y3R1cmUiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6N30= required several jigs to coax the article’s AI-generated code toward the result we wanted. It would’ve taken too long to prompt my way there—if I was able to at all. Making those tools showed me the potential of AI coding agents for designing unique experiences and gave me a new way of thinking about the designer’s role in the midst of increasing automation. Once I made my own jigs, I started seeing them everywhere in AI design tooling.


JIGS IN PRACTICE IN ‘BEFORE THE DELUGE’

When it came time to turn Laura Entis https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiRGVzaWduaW5nIFdpdGggQUk_IE1ha2UgYSBKaWcuIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDQwMiwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vQGxhdXJhXzI3YmJhZl8xIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjh9’s exclusive reporting from inside OpenAI into a published piece, our team settled on the idea of using flows of particles to visually illustrate the article’s flood metaphor.

https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiRGVzaWduaW5nIFdpdGggQUk_IE1ha2UgYSBKaWcuIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDQwMiwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZDI0b3ZoZ3U4czczNDEuY2xvdWRmcm9udC5uZXQvdXBsb2Fkcy9lZGl0b3IvcG9zdC80NDAyL29wdGltaXplZF8xYzQ4OTIzMy1lMGZkLTQ3YWItODBjYy05YThhNTAzMjVkODEuanBnIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjl9An early art direction idea from head of marketing Douglas Brundage. (Images courtesy of ChatGPT/Douglas Brundage.)




Early on, I’d decided to have each line of the article’s prologue scroll up individually, with a steady river of particles wending around them and through the rest of the piece. But it quickly got tedious to tell my coding agent to speed up or slow down the river, or make it more or less dense during this exploratory phase.

So I asked the agent to make me a control panel, embedded on the page, that would allow me to adjust all the parameters hidden in the code itself—like how close the river got to the blocks of text, or the ranges in which the randomly generated particles varied in size and opacity. Playing with these parameters clarified how I wanted the river to feel in order to best support the prose: alive, mysterious, and with a mind of its own.

https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiRGVzaWduaW5nIFdpdGggQUk_IE1ha2UgYSBKaWcuIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDQwMiwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZDI0b3ZoZ3U4czczNDEuY2xvdWRmcm9udC5uZXQvdXBsb2Fkcy9lZGl0b3IvcG9zdC80NDAyL29wdGltaXplZF9mMGUyNjBmMC02MmRiLTRhNWUtOTc1Mi1lZWZhMTI5MDc4ODguanBnIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjEwfQ==Control panels to adjust text elements, particle flow, and drop-cap positioning. (Screenshot courtesy of Jack Cheng.)




I made separate jigs to move and resize blocks of text, and change the spacing of the raised capital letters at the start of each section. The most elaborate of these jigs tuned 27 distinct visual variables in the story section that explains how a deluge of AI-generated code affects a software pipeline—and how OpenAI handles the flood today and is making plans for the future. To show the effects of different actions on the pipeline, each individual step needed its own camera movements, labels, and particle parameters independent of the other steps.

https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49

This is a free preview of a subscribers-only post.

Around here, rumors of a good AI workflow spread quickly. As soon as someone shows off their Codex setup, several other people rush to copy it—until they realize the setup was built around a person, not a job. You can borrow someone’s ideas but not their workload, their brain, or their life.

Plus: The models the team is driving this week, a workflow for making data visualizations, and the race for AI coding supremacy heats up even more.

----------------------------------------




SIGNAL

What happened: After 16 years as CEO of Google DeepMind, Demis Hassabis is transitioning into a new role as chief scientist of Alphabet. Koray Kavukcuoglu, DeepMind’s CTO, will run the lab as senior vice president, overseeing Gemini model development, frontier research, and the Gemini app and developer teams while Hassabis continues as chairman alongside his chief scientist role.

Meanwhile, Meta launched Muse Code, its first terminal coding agent, in beta yesterday. Mark Zuckerberg wrote (on X, ironically) https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQSBDb2RleCBvZiBPbmXigJlzIE93biIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0MDEsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InByb21vIiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS9maW5rZC9zdGF0dXMvMjA4NTA4MDc1MDAzNDk0MDIwMSIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo2fQ== that the harness can tackle “complete software engineering tasks” such as planning, writing, and validating code “across large repos.” In other words, Claude Code or Codex, but make it Meta.

What it means: With OpenAI and Anthropic sprinting ahead in the AI coding race, both DeepMind and Meta have some catching up to do. CEO Dan Shipper https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQSBDb2RleCBvZiBPbmXigJlzIE93biIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0MDEsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InByb21vIiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9AZGFuc2hpcHBlciIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo3fQ== saw in the “tea leaves” https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQSBDb2RleCBvZiBPbmXigJlzIE93biIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0MDEsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InByb21vIiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS9kYW5zaGlwcGVyL3N0YXR1cy8yMDg1MDQ4OTkwODk5MzE1MTQyIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjh9 that Hassabis “believes different fundamental research directions…are more important to his long-term goal,” even if they are “less [important] competitively today.” The personnel shift appears to give the company the best of both worlds: a pragmatic play at the most lucrative space in AI today and a bid at looking farther down the road toward AGI. Meta—under pressure following a lackluster earnings report https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQSBDb2RleCBvZiBPbmXigJlzIE93biIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQ0MDEsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InByb21vIiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuY25iYy5jb20vMjAyNi8wNy8yOS9tZXRhLXEyLWVhcm5pbmdzLXJlcG9ydC0yMDI2Lmh0bWwiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6OX0= in July—seems to be making a similarly practical decision to go where the revenue is.

What to do: Adding Meta and a newly re-dedicated DeepMind to the mix (plus SpaceXAI, which is here, too) brings the total to five different frontier labs gunning for our mindshare and token spend. That’s either an overwhelming amount of choice, or Christmas has come early, depending on your perspective. #### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/1a8122ed-2187-4978-abf7-791b3c1f00dc/1729462902360__1_.png?t=1786026639)
Caption: Demis Hassabis

**1/ Demis Hassabis steps down as Google DeepMind CEO:** Google [reshuffled](https://blog.google/company-news/inside-google/message-ceo/next-chapter-ai-momentum/) its AI leadership, with Demis Hassabis stepping down as CEO to become Chair of Google DeepMind and Alphabet's Chief Scientist while continuing to lead Isomorphic Labs. DeepMind CTO Koray Kavukcuoglu will oversee day-to-day AI development, and longtime Google AI leader Jeff Dean is [leaving](https://x.com/JeffDean/status/2085083442669318443) after 27 years to launch Discovery Loop, a startup focused on automating scientific research.

**2/ Meta enters the coding agent race:** Meta launched [Muse Code](https://research.meta.ai/blog/introducing-muse-code-and-muse-spark-1-2), a beta terminal coding agent powered by its new Muse Spark 1.2 model, taking direct aim at OpenAI's Codex and Anthropic's Claude Code. It can plan, write, and validate code across large repositories using persistent background agents. The model delivers major improvements in coding and agentic reasoning while keeping API pricing unchanged, as Meta continues expanding its AI lineup with lower-cost offerings.

**3/ An OpenAI researcher leaves to build telepathy:** Former OpenAI researcher Naomi Bashkansky [announced](https://naomibashkansky.com/blog/telepathy/) she's joining Conduit to develop thought-to-text AI that translates non-invasive brain signals into text and AI commands. The startup aims to build neural interfaces that let users communicate with AI using their thoughts, with a long-term vision of making AI feel like a natural extension of the human mind.

**4/ Figure AI introduces a web browsing model for everyday tasks:** Figure AI unveiled [Hark Handoff](https://x.com/adcock_brett/status/2085018697312383349?s=20), an AI model designed to navigate the internet like a human by ordering food, booking flights, shopping, and completing other everyday online tasks. The company says independent evaluations rank it ahead of ChatGPT 5.4 and Opus 4.8 on internet use, as it works toward building a digital humanoid that can operate across the web.
